blocks.content: The build context is the set of files Docker actually has access to during a build, usually the entire directory you point docker build at. Instructions like COPY can only reach files inside it.
1. What Gets Sent to the Daemon
blocks.text: 1. What Gets Sent to the Daemon

blocks.content: When you run docker build ., that trailing . is the build context, the entire contents of the current directory are packaged up and sent to the daemon before the build even begins, so it has everything it might need to satisfy COPY or ADD instructions.

blocks.alt: Everything in the context directory gets sent, upfront

blocks.content:
docker build -t myapp .
# "." is the build context: the current directory's
# entire contents are sent to the daemon.

code.content:
docker build -t myapp .
# "." is the build context: the current directory's
# entire contents are sent to the daemon.

codes.bash:
docker build -t myapp .
# "." is the build context: the current directory's
# entire contents are sent to the daemon.

blocks.content: Not everything in a project directory belongs in the build context, node_modules, .git, local environment files. A .dockerignore file, syntactically similar to .gitignore, excludes exactly those paths before the context is even sent.

blocks.alt: .dockerignore keeps unnecessary files out of the context

blocks.content: 3. A Bloated Context Slows Every Build
blocks.text: 3. A Bloated Context Slows Every Build

blocks.content: Because the whole context is sent before the first instruction even runs, an unnecessarily large context (a forgotten multi-gigabyte log directory, an uncommitted node_modules) makes every single build slower to even start, regardless of how good your layer caching is.

blocks.alt: A bloated context is slow before the build has even begun

blocks.title: Key Takeaway
points: The build context is everything in the directory you point docker build at, and COPY/ADD can only reach files inside it.
A .dockerignore file keeps the context lean, which matters for build speed independent of layer caching.
